summary.headline: Page Industries Q2 FY27 sales rose 11.5% to INR 14,396.1 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 20.8% from 21.7% on input inflation; volume up 5.5%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 volume grew 5.5% to 59.8 million pieces and sales value rose 11.5% to INR 14,396.1 million, helped by a 2.5% price increase fully effective in the quarter. EBITDA rose 7.4% to INR 3,001.4 million, with margin at 20.8% versus 21.7%, still within the company's 19%-21% range. H1 volume grew 5.6% against a full-year double-digit guidance that management says is intact, relying on festive-season timing shifts and new Diwali launches. Raw material inflation of about 6.5%-7% YoY persists, and a FEMA non-compliance matter (about INR 48 crore involved) was disclosed with management guiding to minimal operational impact.

segments.name: Men's and women's innerwear, outerwear, athleisure
segments.commentary: Management said athleisure and outerwear, and women's innerwear, will grow a notch above men's innerwear, a pattern seen over three to four years. Men's innerwear and women's outerwear saw the supply shortfalls in Q2.

segments.name: Distribution network
segments.commentary: Ended Q2 with 115,426 multi-brand outlets, 1,662 exclusive brand stores and 921 large-format stores. Company plans to add 8,000-10,000 outlets by FY27 end, versus 7,000-8,000 added in prior years.

segments.name: Speedo (D2C)
segments.commentary: Speedo no longer sold direct to consumers; now served through a third-party franchise model, following the FEMA-related restriction on online sale of imported goods (applied to Jockey products).

guidance_outlook: Full-year volume growth guidance of double digits is maintained; H1 volume grew 5.5%-5.6%, implying about 14%-15% growth needed in H2 per analyst math.
EBITDA margin expected to stay within the 19%-21% planned range in H2 FY27, per CFO.
Management sees Q2 margins as a good indication of the going-forward gross and EBITDA margin, absent further input cost changes or efficiency gains.
S/4HANA go-live planned in Q4 FY27.
Odisha and K.R. Pete plants at about 40% of target output; peak capacity expected by end of FY28, with headcount rising in H2.
No price increase announced beyond the 2.5% from May 2026; management will take it one month at a time while input costs persist.
capex_capacity: Odisha and K.R. Pete plants operating at about 40% of intended capacity; full ramp-up expected in about 1.5 years, reaching peak utilisation by end of FY28.
Headcount to rise in H2 FY27 as the two new plants ramp up, so employee cost is expected to catch up with business.
New distribution centre launched in West Bengal to support D2C in the eastern region for jockey.in and partner marketplaces.
Order fulfilment fell to about 96%-97% from a historical 98%-99%, mainly in men's innerwear and women's outerwear; management targets recovery of 1%-1.5%.
Demand forecasting automation (auto-replenishment) piloted from Q2 across some touchpoints.
demand_pricing: Management said competitive intensity in Q1 and Q2 was subdued versus the last three years, though festive-season consumer offers and discounting were high.
Raw material inflation about 6.5%-7% YoY in Q2 and still at that level in October; cotton and crude-linked inputs remain elevated, with no softening seen.
Price increase of 2.5% effective May 2026 (fully in Q2) partly offset inflation; a further hike will depend on input costs.
July and August primary growth was close to 2x the Q2 headline rate, per management; September dipped on festive timing shift from September to October.
Premiumisation (higher price points within categories, outerwear mix, EBO and online full-price sales) contributed to ASP improvement alongside the 2.5% price hike.
Management declined to share October-November performance.
A three-day billing shortfall at end-June/early-July in Q1 was recovered in July.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company achieve the H2 volume growth needed to meet double-digit full-year guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the festive build-up shifting from September to October-November, new Diwali launches in men's innerwear and bras backed by marketing, and tertiary sales tracking on plan. It said guidance is intact and management is on track against internal plans.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin contract more in Q2 than Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 benefited from inventory pre-positioned in Q4 FY26 at lower costs and the May price increase. Full inflation hit from late June, and the 2.5% price rise only started from July, so the pre-positioned benefit was exhausted in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the FEMA matter and what penalty is possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Involved amount is about INR 48 crore cumulative over roughly 2014-2026. Best estimate is a penalty of about 0.75% of that amount; a 3x penalty is considered extremely unlikely. Management sees no operational impact and the matter is being taken to DPIIT for post-facto approval.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a supply chain issue that cost revenue in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Order fulfilment fell to 96%-97% from 98%-99%, with about 3%-4% primary order loss in men's innerwear and women's outerwear. Management said it has recovered to about 97%-98% and sees the issue as controllable, linked to new-plant ramp-up and imported raw material delays.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins at a bottom, and will EBITDA improve from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is a good indication of margins, with future movement dependent on input costs and efficiency gains. CFO reiterated that H2 EBITDA margin should stay within 19%-21%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost up only 3.9% YoY and what drives wage increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount was described as optimal in H1. Headcount will rise in H2 as Odisha and K.R. Pete ramp up. Karnataka wage revisions for garmenting workers took effect in April and are in the budget; the support-staff revision is sub judice and does not affect garmenting.

risks_watch: Full-year volume guidance requires about 14%-15% growth in H2 against 5.5% in H1; progress on the festive shift is the key swing factor.
Raw material inflation of about 6.5%-7% YoY, with no softening; further price hikes are possible but not committed, and margin is near the lower half of the 19%-21% band if costs stay high.
FEMA non-compliance on imported goods sold online (about INR 48 crore cumulative; penalty estimate about 0.75%); pending DPIIT approval and final outcome not quantified.
Fulfilment rate at 96%-97% versus 98%-99% historically; recovery to 99% still pending, plus SKU-level shortages and imported raw material delays.
Distributor account count and MBO touchpoints declined QoQ for two quarters; management attributes this to cyclical patterns and expects 8,000-10,000 outlet additions in FY27.
Pending contingency on a Middle East partner issue, already disclosed in FY26 annual accounts.
S/4HANA go-live in Q4 FY27 and new plant ramp-ups carry execution risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and full-year volume targets, though they gave no quarter-to-date numbers and deferred pricing decisions with a "wait and watch" stance. Cautious on input costs, which management said have not softened. Evasive on the H2 volume bridge and Q2 revenue lost to supply shortfalls, which they said was unquantified.
key_quotes: As we stand today, the inflated input costs persist.
It's almost a wait and watch to see when we need to effect the price increase.
I would not, in a way, look at it as a structural issue.

adds.what: Odisha and K.R. Pete plants (new, ramping at about 40% of target output)

growth.why: Management maintains double-digit FY27 volume guidance despite H1 volume growth of only 5.5-5.6%, implying roughly 14-15% in H2; backing is partial, relying on the Odisha and K.R. Pete plants ramping to peak by end FY28, festive timing shifts, new Diwali launches and July-August primary growth near 2x the Q2 rate, with no firm order numbers given.

quality.why: Q2 sales rose 11.5% on 5.5% volume growth plus a 2.5% price increase and premiumisation (ASP lift), so the gap between value and volume growth is price/mix rather than one-offs; no one-off gains or low-base effects are cited, but the 11.5% headline is flattered by price and the pre-positioned/price benefit faded in the quarter.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 20.8% in Q2 from 21.7% and H1 margin is 20.6% vs 22%; raw material inflation is still about 6.5%-7% YoY with no softening, and management guides H2 only within 19%-21%, with Q2 as the reference point.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Odisha and K.R. Pete plants are already commissioned but running at about 40% of target output, with headcount rising in H2 FY27 and peak capacity expected by end of FY28; 8,000-10,000 outlet additions are planned by FY27 end versus 7,000-8,000 in prior years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Full-year double-digit guidance is held, but H1 volume grew only 5.6% (121.7 million pieces), so H2 needs about 14%-15%; July-August primary growth was near 2x the Q2 rate of 5.5%, but management gave no October-November data and September dipped.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new capex announcement discussed; the existing Odisha and K.R. Pete plants are still ramping to 40% of target output, which is well below the 80%+ utilisation threshold, so a fresh plant is not implied.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held guidance (double-digit volume, 19%-21% margin) rather than raising it, with H1 volume at 5.6% and input costs still rising 6.5%-7% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Double-digit volume needs about 14%-15% in H2 against 5.6% in H1, and fulfilment has fallen to 96%-97% from 98%-99% with recovery targeted at only 1%-1.5%; management gave no October-November numbers.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited new Diwali launches in men's innerwear and bras backed by marketing, and a Speedo move to a franchise model, though no product count or revenue size was given.

rows.label: Further price hike depends on input costs
rows.why: A 2.5% price increase took effect May 2026 and raw material inflation is still 6.5%-7% YoY, but management has no further hike committed and will decide one month at a time.

rows.label: Fulfilment recovery to 98%-99%
rows.why: Fulfilment fell to 96%-97% from 98%-99% and management says it has recovered to about 97%-98% with a target of 1%-1.5% more, which would lift lost primary orders.

rows.label: FEMA matter resolution via DPIIT
rows.why: About INR 48 crore is involved and the best-estimate penalty is about 0.75% (roughly INR 36 lakh), with the matter going to DPIIT for post-facto approval and management seeing no operational impact.

tone.note: Management was confident on full-year double-digit volume, the 19%-21% margin band and the Odisha and K.R.
